clue.text: Frown on the use of awfully vapid prose

indicators.note: awfully suggests the words are badly put together, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic disapproves of someone writing in an insipid style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' signals an anagram of VAPID PROSE; 'the use of' just links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown on something is to show you think badly of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Many refuse to speed

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, many
ash is refuse left after burning

explanation.surface: Lots of rubbish is in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to rush or hurry, a synonym of speed.

clue.text: Separating if in smart environment

indicators.note: environment means the word for smart surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to sting is to smart with pain

explanation.surface: Sorting out a stylish setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' reads as an adjective meaning stylish, but here it is the verb meaning to hurt; 'environment' is the container signal and 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sifting is sorting by passing through a sieve, separating fine from coarse.

clue.text: To re-use props may be quite ridiculous

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Recycling stage props might seem absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-use' looks like the anagram signal, but the fodder is the whole of TO RE-USE PROPS, with 'may be' as indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposterous means absurd, utterly contrary to reason.

clue.text: Very much behind, so raise the maximum

parts.note: to rear is to raise up
most means the greatest amount

explanation.surface: Far behind, so increase the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means furthest back, last of all.

clue.text: Empty one container into another

indicators.note: into says the first pieces are put inside the other container

parts.note: another container: a vat is a large tank
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: Instructions to pour one vessel into another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like an imperative verb but is the adjective definition; A and CAN go into VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacant means unoccupied, holding nothing.

clue.text: Expert in cable TV

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words cable TV

explanation.surface: Someone is a specialist in cable television.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is tucked inside 'cABLE Tv', signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An able person is skilled or competent, close to expert as an adjective.

clue.text: A coal-burning vessel

parts.note: reads like a steamship fuelled by coal, but means a metal container in which a fire burns

explanation.surface: A steamship powered by coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable metal stand holding burning coals is literally a coal-burning container.

clue.text: Tip over cross put in unsafe position

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: end means tip, as in the tip of a finger
cross means angry, so angered

explanation.surface: Tipping over a crucifix could leave it precarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangered means placed at risk, threatened.

clue.text: The badge of all his tribe, Shylock declared

definitions.text: The badge of all his tribe, Shylock declared

parts.words: The badge of all his tribe, Shylock declared
parts.note: a quotation from The Merchant of Venice: Shylock says patient endurance is the badge of all our tribe

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's moneylender about what marks out his people.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock, in The Merchant of Venice, says 'For sufferance is the badge of all our tribe'; the clue asks you to fill the missing word of the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient tolerance of ill treatment is what Shylock names as his people's mark.

clue.text: A poet quite the reverse of cheerless

indicators.note: quite the reverse of tells us to read the word for cheerless backwards

parts.note: drab means dull and cheerless

explanation.surface: A poet who is the very opposite of gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite the reverse of' looks like a statement of opposite meaning, but it turns DRAB backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a traditional term for a poet, especially a minstrel.

clue.text: They move the furniture in spirited fashion

definitions.text: They move the furniture in spirited fashion

parts.words: They move the furniture in spirited fashion
parts.note: reads like lively removal men, but spirited means done by ghosts, noisy spirits throwing objects about

explanation.surface: Energetic removal men shifting furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy ghosts are reputed to move objects about a house.

clue.text: Pygmalion's sister got nothing done

parts.note: did is the past form of do, so done = carried out
O is the letter shaped like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The sister of a legendary figure achieved nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Shaw's Pygmalion: in legend Pygmalion, king of Tyre, was the brother of the queen of Carthage loved by Aeneas.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical legend the founder queen of Carthage was the sister of King Pygmalion of Tyre.

clue.text: Possibly causing gloom in an Oriental

indicators.note: possibly causing suggests the letters could produce something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that might make an Eastern person feel gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly causing' signals an anagram of GLOOM IN AN; the final 'an' is fodder, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Asian steppe nation north of China is an Easterner, an example of an Oriental.

clue.text: Holy music composed by simple church worker

parts.note: plain means simple
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: Sacred music written by a humble church employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied liturgical chant, such as Gregorian, is sacred music.

clue.text: Most bright, so taking the least trouble

definitions.meaning: superlative of light in the sense of bright, luminous
superlative of light in the sense of easy, not heavy or demanding

explanation.surface: The brightest of options is also the one requiring least effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means both bright and undemanding, so its superlative covers most luminous and least burdensome.

clue.text: A writer given strict direction

parts.note: stern means strict or severe
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: An author receives severe instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century novelist Laurence Sterne is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Some' go wrong, note, in making beds

parts.note: part means some of something
to err is to go wrong
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Some things go awry when making the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making beds' suggests bedrooms; it is the garden kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal ornamental garden laid out as flower beds and paths.

clue.text: Naughty child seen by the river getting dirty

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A mischievous child by the riverbank gets filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Impure means contaminated or unclean, a synonym of dirty.

clue.text: Knight-errant finding a youngster in distress

indicators.note: in says the youngster sits inside the word for distress

parts.note: pain means distress or suffering
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A wandering knight discovers a young person in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'youngster' is only a link word, since the A in the answer comes from the word for distress; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Paladins were Charlemagne's peers, hence any chivalrous knight on a quest.

clue.text: Bearing the cost of transportation

explanation.surface: Who pays the shipping charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's deportment and the fee paid for conveying goods.

clue.text: Inane, is, put another way, stupid

indicators.note: put another way suggests the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Inane, in other words, means stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a thesaurus entry; 'put another way' signals an anagram of INANE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish, like an ass.

clue.text: Various people going down

parts.note: reads like a mixed group descending, but the Var is one such flowing thing and these all run downhill to the sea

explanation.surface: An assortment of people descending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' hides the Var, a French watercourse; the things meant all flow downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercourses flow downward from source to sea.

clue.text: Making a painter frown, one is taken in charge

indicators.note: is taken in says the following pieces go inside the word for charge

parts.note: cost means a charge or price
lour means to frown or scowl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an arrest, but it is the price; 'is taken in' is the container signal, and 'Making' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in the use of colour is a kind of painter.

clue.text: Formerly it could offer a way out

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: Something that once might have provided an escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a door or passage by which one leaves.

clue.text: Tie for a flier

definitions.meaning: a fastening made by looping string
a wading bird of the sandpiper family

explanation.surface: Neckwear for a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fastening tied in rope and a sandpiper-like shore bird.

clue.text: Minister filling, in for tots

indicators.note: filling says the minister's letters go inside the word for in

parts.note: as can mean in the role of, so in
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a qualified minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman stands in as a substitute for small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tots' looks like children but is the verb, as in totting up; DD (Doctor of Divinity) fills AS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to sum figures, a synonym.

clue.text: The pit's' economic decline

definitions.meaning: a hollow or sunken place in the ground
a long severe slump in trade

explanation.surface: The coal mine's financial slump.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hollow in the ground and a severe economic slump.

clue.text: Temporary leader — 'close watch is required

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Temporary

parts.note: end means close or conclusion

explanation.surface: An acting leader must be watched closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to look after or mind, so to watch over.

clue.text: The, estimation of free men's assets

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose to form a new order

explanation.surface: Valuing the property of liberated people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like an adjective for men, but it signals an anagram of MENS ASSETS.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation or judgement, a synonym of estimation.
